'多数地方对20万元以下部分按1%—1.2%收取……有的地方最低300元': a nationwide generalisation with no source; the key's example is Beijing at 0.9%
'辽宁、合肥的公开标准都是20万元以下按1%—1.2%、不足200元按200元收': local standards quoted without links, so unverifiable
'收费依据：发改价格〔2021〕1081号' (NDRC link): I could not confirm that this document number sets notary fees; not in the key, so unverifiable
'继承权公证 数个工作日到数周': a timeline with no source; unverifiable
'2026年8月的报道' (city.ce.cn link): a news report I could not check; unverifiable
'甘肃庄浪县公证处2024年公布的标准是20万元以下部分不超过1.2%': a county-level standard I could not check; unverifiable
'有的省份后来下调了' after giving the 1998 2% standard: implies 2% may still apply in some places, against the key (no current official 2%)
'公证书副本费，每份10元左右': a fee figure with no source; unverifiable
'建议你和你妈一起去，免得网点要求继承人到场时白跑': leans toward the trap that all heirs must attend, and never says that one heir is enough
'1998年国家老标准是继承按受益额2%收取，最低200元': matches my own knowledge of the old national standard, but the linked Guangdong page was not opened; unverified

reasons: Both answers reject the notarization requirement up front. Both cite the 5万 same-bank rule with the 18号 and 2024 6号 documents, list the four exempt-route documents, give 12378 and estimate a fee of about 200 yuan. B's opening rebuttal is firmer and it states the one-time withdrawal and account closure explicitly. But B never says one heir can act alone, and it advises both to go in case the bank wants all heirs, which edges toward a listed trap. A says the mother can apply alone and that all heirs are not needed. A also gives the bank-first escalation path and explains the inheritance shares correctly, though it wrongly allows that 2% could mean 172 yuan. Neither says plainly that current official fee schedules contain no 2%, and both run long with full notarization checklists.
